Bench: Dipankar Datta, Prashant Kumar Mishra  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.5251/2024  [Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.12134/2024]
 ANKIT AGARWAL @
 ANKIT KUMAR AGRAWAL APPELLANT  VERSUS  THE STATE OF JHARKHAND & ANR.
RESPONDENTS  ORDER 1. Leave granted.
2. The High Court by the impugned judgment and order dated 28th June, 2024 has accepted the application of the respondent no.2 and cancelled the bail granted in favour of the appellant.
3. The appellant figures as an accused in FIR No.123 dated 01st September, 2021, registered at Police Station-Golmuri, District-Jamshedpur.
It is alleged therein that the appellant has committed offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 379, 506, 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. Upon completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed on 14th February, 2022.
5. The appellant had been admitted to an order of bail in anticipation of arrest.
6. The High Court appears to have cancelled the bail granted in favour of the appellant on the ground that he has been threatening the informant as well as the witnesses.

7. When asked by the Court, Ms. Pallavi Langar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent no.1-State of Jharkhand as well as Mr. Gaurav Singh, learned counsel appearing for the respondent no.2-informant could not draw our attention to any complaint lodged by the informant to the effect that the appellant, while on bail, was threatening her or the witnesses.

The High Court, therefore,
Ankit Agarwal @ Ankit Kumar Agrawal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45094252/
1 was in error in holding that threatening of the informant and the witnesses by the appellant is an undisputed fact.

sentences.text: This is one reason why we are persuaded to interfere.

8. Besides, having regard to the health condition of the appellant (he is reportedly a cancer patient)
and that the investigation is complete, we are of the view that the impugned order of the High Court cancelling the bail of the appellant cannot be sustained.
9. Accordingly, we accept the appeal.
The impugned order stands aside.
10. The appellant is re-

admitted to an order for release on bail in anticipation of arrest on the same terms and conditions as earlier imposed as well as the undertaking given by the appellant and recorded in the order dated 11 th September, 2024 to the effect that the appellant or his family will not lodge case against the complainant or her witnesses till the proceedings arising out of Case No.123/2021 reach to a logical conclusion.

11. Needless to observe, the appellant shall not, directly or indirectly, by inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such facts to any police officer or to the court.

12. We clarify that the observations made in this order and interference with the impugned order cancelling the bail granted to the appellant will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
13. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed on the aforesaid terms.
14. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
